findings.title: Duplicate charge on request retry
findings.hypothesis: A client that retries a failed or timed-out POST /payment will trigger a second charge_card call because there is no cache lookup before the external call, so the same card is charged twice with no deduplication.
evidence: inventory.json > idempotency_patterns[0]: first_cache_read_line=null (cache is never read before the external call)
inventory.json > idempotency_patterns[0]: first_external_call_line=33 (charge_card called at app/payment.py:33)
inventory.json > idempotency_patterns[0]: first_cache_write_line=48 (cache.set written only after charge, at app/payment.py:48)
findings.verification_note: Fixed in app/payment.py: process_payment() now computes a deterministic idempotency key via hashlib.sha256(user_id:amount:currency) and calls cache.get() before charge_card(). Confirmed by tests/test_verification_gaps.py::test_fh01_no_duplicate_charge_on_retry PASSING. inventory.json now shows cache_checked_before_external_call=true, first_cache_read_line=38, first_external_call_line=42.

findings.title: Race condition on shared balance under concurrent requests
findings.hypothesis: Two concurrent payment requests for the same user can both read the same pre-deduction balance from the unprotected _balances dict, pass the funds check, and both write back a reduced balance — effectively allowing a double-spend up to the full account balance.
evidence: inventory.json > shared_mutable_state[1]: read_lines=[20, 24] (balance read in get_balance at :20 and in charge_card at :24)
inventory.json > shared_mutable_state[1]: write_lines=[27] (balance decremented at app/payment.py:27)
inventory.json > functions[charge_card]: calls_in_order=[_balances.get, InsufficientFundsError, uuid.uuid4] — read and write are non-atomic

findings.title: Card charged with no order record if database write fails
findings.hypothesis: If save_order raises an exception after charge_card has already returned a charge_id, the charge is irrecoverable — no order is persisted, no rollback or compensation is performed, and the customer's funds are lost with no record.
evidence: inventory.json > functions[process_payment]: calls_in_order=[charge_card, uuid.uuid4, save_order, cache.set]
inventory.json > functions[process_payment].calls_with_lines: charge_card at app/payment.py:33, save_order at app/payment.py:37
inventory.json > functions[save_order]: calls_in_order=[Order, db.add, db.commit, db.refresh] — db.commit (durability point) is at app/database.py:43, after charge_card has already run

findings.title: Cache store (_store) has no lock protection under concurrency
findings.hypothesis: The in-memory _store dict used for idempotency caching has no lock, so concurrent writes can interleave and produce a torn or stale cache entry, undermining whatever idempotency protection cache.set is intended to provide.
evidence: inventory.json > shared_mutable_state[0]: read_lines=[7] (cache.get reads _store at app/cache.py:7)
inventory.json > shared_mutable_state[0]: write_lines=[11] (cache.set writes _store at app/cache.py:11)
